# Wakaru

> Wakaru is a JavaScript decompiler. It splits production bundles into modules and restores readable, modern syntax from minified and transpiled code. It runs locally as a CLI (`npx wakaru`) and reads its input without executing it.

Wakaru is not a deobfuscator. For obfuscated input, strip the obfuscation first with a dedicated tool such as webcrack, then run Wakaru on the result.

## Docs

- [Docs index](https://wakarujs.com/docs/llms.txt): every docs page with a one-line summary
- [Full docs](https://wakarujs.com/docs/llms-full.txt): all docs pages in one file
- [Quick Start](https://wakarujs.com/docs): decompile a file or unpack a bundle
- [Unminify a webpack bundle](https://wakarujs.com/docs/guides/unminify-a-webpack-bundle): from a production build to readable modules
- [Unminify a file](https://wakarujs.com/docs/guides/unminify-a-file): one minified or transpiled file to readable JavaScript
- [Unpack a bundle](https://wakarujs.com/docs/guides/unpack-a-bundle): split a bundle into modules
- [CLI reference](https://wakarujs.com/docs/reference/cli): every command and flag
- [Supported inputs](https://wakarujs.com/docs/reference/supported-inputs): bundlers, transpilers, and minifiers Wakaru understands
- [Coding agents](https://wakarujs.com/docs/guides/coding-agents): install the Wakaru skill for a coding agent

## Optional

- [Playground](https://wakarujs.com/playground/): try Wakaru in the browser, no install
- [GitHub](https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru): source, issues, and releases
- [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/wakaru): the `wakaru` package
